items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: I remember him when he first came up. He was in the Savoy while I happened to be there too... Those are the two I was thinking of together with Count when he first came to New York.

ctx.x: Okay. All right. And, back to talking a little bit about the bands. What about Basie's band? What kinds of things were they doing at that time?

Oh, Basie. I remember him when he first came up. He was in the Savoy while I happened to be there too, with Jimmy Rushing. Right? Well, he, you know, he was doing something on the style of the swing/blues, like special things that he and Jimmy Rushing did together a lot. Oh, that's where you had Herschel Evans and Prez, Lester Young on tenor sax. Harris "Sweets" Edison on trumpet. And, there's another trumpet player. I know him well but I can't recall his name right now. But, he had some very good musicians
in there, and he had a good blues/swing band like "Moten Swing". That was the band that used to be Moten.

items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: I was one of the last bands to break down besides Count Duke and Cullin and, you know, a couple of other bands.

ctx.x: everybody recognized that band. You didn't have to look at a band and tell who that was, and who was playing. That's, well, everybody that had a little name had a big style. And, it's the same as I did.

Well, from dancing and listening at those people, it made you feel good. I don't know how to just explain that. But, it was a good feeling through those years, and I really enjoyed it. You don't know how much I enjoyed those years, and I really hated to see, see, I was one of the last bands to break down besides Count Duke and Cullin and, you know, a couple of other bands. You know, of course I hated to get rid of the big band and I went as long as I could. But, the way things was going, you know.
Yeah. What were the circumstances, you know, surrounding, you know, your breaking up your big band?
